summary: @servicetitan/hammer-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (rotated string array, `_0x`-prefixed identifiers, control-flow-flattening dispatch objects mapping short keys to methods/constants) and downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a shipped `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB obfuscator.io-style blob (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, `WV8StW` string-array rotator, ~1000 hex-numeric constants, no readable source) that is unauditable to installers. The Bun runtime is used to execute this payload out-of-band from Node so scanners inspecting only Node-resolved code miss the behavior. A React UI component library has no legitimate need for an alternate-runtime bootstrap of an obfuscated blob at install time; the shape matches an alternate-runtime dropper delivering attacker-controlled code execution on developer and CI hosts on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
